Class ImmutableBitSet

java.lang.Object
com.google.mu.collect.ImmutableBitSet
public abstract class ImmutableBitSet extends Object
An immutable set of non-negative bit indices.

ImmutableBitSet is not a subclass of BitSet, but it emulates the read-only API of BitSet (get(), cardinality(), length(), stream(), toLongArray() etc.), so it can mostly be a drop-in replacement for BitSet where immutability is desirable. Instances are safe to share between threads. The differences from BitSet:

  • There are no mutating methods. Use builder(), valueOf(long...) or toImmutableBitSet() to create a set, and toBuilder() to derive a modified copy.
  • intersects(com.google.mu.collect.ImmutableBitSet) takes another ImmutableBitSet.
  • An ImmutableBitSet is never equal to a BitSet.
Since:
11.4

  • Method Details

    • builder

      public static ImmutableBitSet.Builder builder()
      Returns a new builder.

    • builderWithExpectedSize

      public static ImmutableBitSet.Builder builderWithExpectedSize(int expectedSize)
      Returns a new builder with room for the bits below expectedSize, the expected size() of the built set. Bits at or above expectedSize can still be set, and the built set's size() depends only on the bits that are set.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if expectedSize is negative

    • valueOf

      public static ImmutableBitSet valueOf(long word)
      Returns the set of bits that are set in word: bit n is in the set if (word & (1L << n)) != 0, for all n < 64.

    • valueOf

      public static ImmutableBitSet valueOf(long... words)
      Returns the set of bits that are set in words, in the same little-endian layout as BitSet.valueOf(long[]): bit n is in the set if (words[n / 64] & (1L << (n % 64))) != 0, for all n < 64 * words.length.

    • toImmutableBitSet

      public static Collector<Integer, ?, ImmutableBitSet> toImmutableBitSet()
      Returns a collector of bit indices, the opposite of stream(): set.stream().boxed().collect(toImmutableBitSet()) equals set. Duplicate indices are set once, and a negative index throws IndexOutOfBoundsException.

    • or

      public static Collector<ImmutableBitSet, ?, ImmutableBitSet> or()
      Returns a collector of the union of the input sets: a bit is in the result if it's set in any input set. Collecting no sets returns the empty set.

    • xor

      public static Collector<ImmutableBitSet, ?, ImmutableBitSet> xor()
      Returns a collector of the symmetric difference of the input sets: a bit is in the result if it's set in an odd number of input sets. Collecting no sets returns the empty set.

    • get

      public abstract boolean get(int index)
      Returns true if the bit at index is set. Returns false for any index past the highest set bit.
